seo.title: What is DNS?
seo.description: DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it.

definition: DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it.
answerBlock: DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it. Every website visit starts with that lookup. It also decides where your email goes, which is why a careless change can take down more than the site.

body.heading: Why does DNS matter during a launch?
paragraphs: A launch is usually a DNS change: the domain stops pointing at the old server and starts pointing at the new one. Records carry a time to live, the period other systems are allowed to keep the old answer, so lowering it a day before the switch makes the change take effect in minutes rather than hours.

The records that matter are few. A and AAAA records point the domain at a server. CNAME records point one name at another. MX records route email. TXT records carry the verification and mail-authentication entries that stop your messages being marked as spam.

Who controls the domain registration is a question worth settling before launch day, not during it. The account should be in the client company's name, with the agency holding access rather than ownership.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: DNS is the single point of failure most companies have never audited. If the only person with the login left two years ago, that is a launch risk and a security risk at the same time.
It is also where migrations quietly break email, because mail records are copied last or not at all.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Before a migration we lower the time to live, copy every existing record including mail and verification entries, switch, then confirm that both the site and email are answering from the new configuration.

service.title: Website care plans
service.line: Patching, backups with a tested restore, monitoring and a fixed allowance of development hours.

terms.definition: A backup is a copy of the site and its database held somewhere else, and a restore is the rehearsed process of putting that copy back.
A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor.
A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them.
A TLS certificate is the file that lets a website prove who it is and encrypt the traffic between it and the visitor.
